# sce_forge_runtime — header-only algorithm and HAL library for code
# generated by SCE Forge (filter, interpolation, lookup, timer, observer kinds),
# and the checked arithmetic, optional values and spans the statechart
# generator's C++ names (`sce/forge/algorithm.h`, `sce/forge/optional.h`,
# `sce/forge/span.h`).
#
# Policy: see SCE_FORGE.md §2.1
#   - Static linking only, no dynamic dependencies
#   - No stateful global services (no heap, no threads, no I/O in the library)
#   - Header-only templates and pure-virtual interfaces only
#
# The one definition of the target. The top-level CMakeLists.txt adds this
# directory, links the target into `sce_core` (so every SCE tier carries it to
# whatever links that tier, generated code included), installs the headers
# under `include/sce/forge` and exports the target in `SCE_CoreTargets` as
# `SCE::sce_forge_runtime`. The alias below is that same name, so a project
# that adds SCE as a subdirectory and one that finds an installed SCE spell the
# target alike. The Forge harnesses under `tests/` are standalone projects and
# name the include directory themselves.
#
# The interface is C++17 (docs/adr/0059, section 1): a consumer compiles these
# headers at its own standard, and SCE never raises it above C++17.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)

include(GNUInstallDirs)

add_library(sce_forge_runtime INTERFACE)
add_library(SCE::sce_forge_runtime ALIAS sce_forge_runtime)

target_include_directories(sce_forge_runtime INTERFACE
    $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
    $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}>
)

target_compile_features(sce_forge_runtime INTERFACE cxx_std_17)
